variants.name: Live signal: JCI, rupiah, INDOGB 10Y trend, INDOGB–UST spread
US 10Y trend in place of the INDOGB trend
Korea-style rotation (JCI inverted: stocks down = bonds up)

ust.method: Overnight = New York closes strictly before each Jakarta close (New York shuts at about 04:00–05:00 Jakarta). Hedged = INDOGB 10Y minus β × US 10Y, β the trailing 26-week weekly beta known at the time. All variants walk-forward, z-scores vs trailing 52 weeks, thresholds ±0.5, hit rates over the next 4 weeks. The 'Beta 3Y' slot carries the INDOGB 15Y.

src: Yahoo Finance: IDX Composite (^JKSE) and USD/IDR (IDR=X) daily closes; any USD/IDR close more than 1.5% from Bank Indonesia’s JISDOR fix is replaced by JISDOR. INDOGB 10Y: PHEI IGSYC (CNBC benchmark 10Y before the first stored PHEI day). US Treasury daily par yields (2Y, 10Y; home.treasury.gov). Weekly, last trading day of each week.

method.window: 4-week changes; z-scores vs trailing 52 weeks (min 26); thresholds ±0.5
components: USD/IDR 4-week % change (inverted: a weaker rupiah is bond-bearish)
INDOGB − UST 10Y spread vs its 26-week average (wide = cheap)

method.window: 20-day changes; z-scores vs trailing 260 sessions (min 130); spread vs its 130-day average; thresholds ±0.5; hit rates over the next 20 sessions; UST hedge β = trailing 130-day daily beta
components: INDOGB − UST 10Y spread vs its 130-day average (wide = cheap)

notes.headline: The rupiah steadies (JISDOR 18,103) and the JCI adds 0.5%, so the daily signal climbs to −0.49 and leaves sell-off for neutral; the 10Y INDOGB eases to 7.69%, still 52bp higher in four weeks and mostly not explained by Treasuries. Signal −0.49: neutral
notes.now: Foreign money is still out of Indonesian stocks over the month, but the pressure has eased. The JCI rose 0.46% to 5,074 with foreigners net buyers of about Rp104bn by midday (who bought is not disclosed), yet it is 17.5% down over 20 sessions and 44% below its one-year peak; last week foreigners also sold Rp2.29tn of SBN, so October's bond inflows did not carry into November. The rupiah has stopped falling: JISDOR fixed at 18,103 and its 20-session change is down to +0.55% as the early-October slide drops out of the window. That moved the daily signal to −0.49 from −0.94, just inside neutral: the JCI part (z −1.90) and the 10Y trend part (z +1.77, the 10Y up 49bp over 20 sessions) still point to a sell-off, the rupiah part is flat (z −0.18), and the spread part is bond-bullish (z +1.54), with INDOGBs paying 283bp over Treasuries, 42bp above their 130-day average and in the 96th percentile of 52 weeks; that is a nominal pick-up before currency risk. Treasuries explain little of the trend: the US 10Y fell 24bp in four weeks and the 26-week weekly beta is −0.21, so about +5bp of the 52bp four-week rise is the Treasury-linked part and +47bp is residual, which is what the US move does not explain rather than proof of domestic selling or political risk. On the day the link was weak again: Friday's 2bp New York sell-off after strong payrolls implied about +0.7bp for INDOGBs at the 1-year daily beta of 0.34, yet the 10Y fell 1.5bp; INDOGBs follow large US moves in the same direction about 73% of the time, smaller ones much less reliably. The sell-off episode that began Oct 7 ended with the 10Y 52bp higher, a hit so far, though it is still inside its 20-session scoring window. On the daily build since June 2022 the signal scores a Sharpe of 0.75 outright and 0.90 hedged against Treasuries, with sell-off calls right 51% and rally calls 58% over the next 20 sessions; these are in-sample back-tests. Our read for the next 2–4 weeks: neutral on duration rather than short, since a neutral reading has historically come with a small average 20-session move, and in about ten sessions the window drops the pre-MSCI levels, which would lift the signal further at unchanged prices; the MSCI review and BI on Nov 17–18 are the risks that could send it back below −0.5.
notes.flip: The daily signal is neutral between −0.5 and +0.5 and sits at −0.49, so it can slip back to sell-off on a small move: roughly, JISDOR back above 18,200, a new JCI low below 4,900 or the 10Y above its 7.72% high. A move to bond rally (above +0.5) needs a JCI rebound and a firmer rupiah together, the pattern that started the April 2025 rally. The policy triggers are a BI-Rate hike that steadies the rupiah (bearish for the front end on the day, bullish for the trend after) or MSCI softening its Standalone proposal.
phases: JCI 6,500–7,250 while the 10Y rose from 6.2% to a 7.58% peak in October 2022 as global rates surged; stocks held up on the commodity boom.

JCI 6,630–7,380 and 10Y 6.19–7.21%. Stocks and bonds drifted without a clear link; on the weekly build the signal's calls lost money (Sharpe −0.3 from 2022 to August 2024), while the daily build did better over the same span.
JCI fell from 7,812 to 6,258 while the 10Y rose from 6.43% to 7.19%: stocks, rupiah and bonds sold off together, the pattern the signal is built for. Its record improves sharply from here.
JCI climbed from 6,262 to a record 9,075 on Jan 15, 2026, and the 10Y fell to 5.93% in October 2025 as foreign money returned and BI eased.

MSCI froze Indonesian index changes in January and on Oct 15 proposed Standalone status; BI hiked 100bp to 5.75% by June and now weighs more, while a wiretapping case against senior police officers adds political risk. JCI −44% from its peak to about 5,070, 10Y up to 7.69%: the second and deeper foreign exit, though foreigners still bought SBN in October. On Nov 9 the daily signal left sell-off for neutral as the rupiah steadied.
notes.caveats: These are proxies, not reported fund flows: daily foreign SBN holdings (DJPPR) and equity flows (IDX) are not machine-readable for the dashboard, so the rupiah and the JCI stand in for foreign money, and any statement about who bought or sold is a hypothesis. USD/IDR is Yahoo's close, replaced by Bank Indonesia's JISDOR fix on any day it strays more than 1.5% (Yahoo printed ~17,480 from Nov 3, 2026 while JISDOR was ~18,100). Before Oct 29, 2026 the 10Y is CNBC's benchmark-bond yield rather than PHEI's IGSYC, with repeated stale prints removed. The daily back-test runs from June 2022 (957 sessions): the live signal makes 192bp outright (Sharpe 0.75) and 222bp hedged against Treasuries (Sharpe 0.90), against −40bp for always holding the 10Y; the weekly build scores 0.33 and 0.44. Variants that use the US 10Y trend score up to 0.73 outright and 0.78 hedged on the weekly build but were picked after the fact and are not live. In-sample, no trading costs; not a trading system.
